purpose: Smoke-test / template workflow ("Workflow End Happy", category VMware.PSCoE) whose only job is to start at a scripted decision item and terminate normally. It takes no inputs, produces no outputs, touches no vCenter/plugin object, calls no action or nested workflow, and reads/writes no external system. Its sole runtime behaviour is: evaluate the custom condition `return true;` at item1 (display name "initiateWorkflow"), which is a constant, and follow the true edge to end item `item0`, which ends the run with end_mode "0" (normal completion, no exception thrown). The false edge to a second normal end item (`item2`) exists in the graph but is unreachable because the condition is a literal `true`. The workflow declares one workflow-scope attribute, `endMode` (number, value null), which no item binds to or reads — it is dead state. Effectively this is a single-branch no-op that always succeeds.

decisions.item: item1 (custom-condition, display name "initiateWorkflow", root_item / entry point)
decisions.condition: JavaScript body is exactly `return true;` — a constant with no inputs, no in_bindings, and no reference to the `endMode` attribute, so it evaluates to boolean true on every execution

branches.does: item0 is an `end` item with end_mode "0": the workflow finishes normally (state COMPLETED). No outputs are set, nothing is thrown.

branches.when: condition is false (alt_out_name / false arm — structurally present, dynamically unreachable given `return true;`)
branches.does: item2 is also an `end` item with end_mode "0": identical normal completion. The two end items are behaviourally indistinguishable.

side_effects: None. No file, network, vCenter/plugin, configuration-element, resource-element, or logging side effects. No `System.log`/`System.warn` calls, no attribute writes (the `endMode` attribute is never assigned), no in_bindings or out_bindings anywhere in the graph.

Exit semantics: both terminal items use end_mode "0", so the workflow always ends normally; there is no end_mode "1" item, therefore this workflow can never throw a workflow-level exception by design. No catch_name (error handler) is set on any item, so an unexpected runtime error in the condition script would propagate as a failed run rather than being handled.
assumptions: `end_mode` "0" is interpreted as normal workflow completion and "1" as throw/error end; both end items here are "0".
A `custom-condition` item's script returning a truthy value routes to `out_name` and a falsy value routes to `alt_out_name`; `return true;` therefore always routes to item0.

The false arm (item1 → item2) is preserved in the spec as graph structure for fidelity, but a converted implementation would never execute it; a faithful conversion may keep it as an explicit unreachable branch or collapse it, as long as the observable behaviour (normal completion, no output) is unchanged.
The `endMode` attribute is genuinely unused rather than referenced indirectly — there is no scripting in the workflow other than `return true;`, and no bindings exist that could read or write it.

open_questions.question: Must the unused workflow attribute `endMode` (type number, initial value null) be carried over into the converted artifact, or can it be dropped as dead state?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If this workflow is a fixture used to assert round-trip fidelity of attribute declarations (the name suggests it pairs with an 'unhappy'/throwing variant that does use endMode), silently dropping the attribute would break that assertion; if it is only functional behaviour that matters, keeping it adds noise.

open_questions.question: Is the intent of this fixture to exercise the two-distinct-end-items case (a branch converging on separate normal ends), such that a conversion collapsing item0 and item2 into one exit would be considered wrong?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It determines whether tests should assert on graph shape (two terminal nodes, one branch) or only on observable behaviour (runs, completes normally, no output) — the two ends are behaviourally identical, so only structural tests can tell them apart.

confidence_reason: The entire graph is three items with a single literal script (`return true;`), no bindings, no inputs/outputs, no action or nested-workflow calls, no plugin types, and no SDK calls — the runtime behaviour is fully determined by the supplied JSON with nothing hidden behind an external action or sub-workflow. The only residual uncertainty is intent (why the dead `endMode` attribute and the unreachable second end exist), not behaviour.
